title: stdio or remote HTTP?
intro: A transport handles how messages move between client and server. Sort each trait by where it belongs.

cards.text: The client launches the server as a subprocess
Declared in config as a command + args (uv run …, npx …)
Auth is typically handled with environment variables
Dies with its client session and is simply relaunched next time
Must already be running before any client connects
Reached by URL — append /sse (or /mcp/ for streamable HTTP)
Can run stateless (independent requests) or stateful (workflow memory)
Can authorize users via OAuth 2.1 (since the March 2025 spec)

debrief: stdio is the local story: the client owns the server's lifecycle — spawns it from a command in the config, talks over standard I/O, passes secrets as env vars, relaunches at will. Remote HTTP flips ownership: the server is independent infrastructure with a URL (/sse for HTTP+SSE, /mcp/ for streamable HTTP), it must be up before clients arrive, it chooses stateless vs stateful (streamable HTTP allows both — FastMCP('research', stateless_http=True)), and it authenticates properly (OAuth 2.1). Same FastMCP code either way — the transport is a deploy-time decision.
